h1:
Surin Mookata
10 Best BBQ Buffet Spots for Value
intro: Ask anyone in Surin what's for dinner and a common answer in a lot of households is "let's go for mookata." You can sit for hours, order once for the whole table, and keep the per-head budget easy to control. Surin has buffet spots starting at just over a hundred baht, decades-old grilled-beef joints, plus Korean BBQ and pay-by-weight places. We've picked the spots locals talk about most, with the neighborhood, rough price, and opening hours, so you can match one to tonight's plan.

blocks.html: Most mookata in Surin is a fixed per-head buffet: pay once and keep refilling. That suits a family dinner or a big group of friends. The main spots cluster around the town center, near the Elephant Show grounds, behind Surin Rajabhat University, and along Chang Phueak Canal. For grilled beef and Korean BBQ there are several options too. We've ordered them by how well they fit different occasions and budgets, not by claiming one is objectively the best, because the right dipping sauce and grill marinade come down to personal taste. Go try a few and you'll find your own regular.

blocks.text: Mookata & BBQ spots locals go to in Surin

items.name: Tang Tao Mookata Buffet (by the Elephant Show grounds)
items.blurb: The spot people in Surin think of first when they want good-value mookata. You can pile your plate as much as you like with no time limit on your table, and the per-head price includes free drinks, dessert, and ice cream. The location by the Elephant Show grounds is easy to find with convenient parking. Good for a dinner where you want to sit and chat for a long time.
items.meta: By the Elephant Show grounds, Mueang Surin · no time limit

items.name: Mik Grilled Beef Buffet (behind Rajabhat Surin)
items.blurb: A legendary buffet for students and the younger crowd in town. There's a lot to choose from at one price — sliced pork, squid, salmon belly — and it's an unlimited-time buffet, so you can take it easy. It sits behind Surin Rajabhat University and packs out most evenings.
items.meta: Behind Surin Rajabhat Univ. · no time limit

items.name: Ruean Racha Grilled BBQ
items.blurb: An old grilled-beef joint that locals call a Surin legend. It's been on Sirirat Road for years, and what people talk about is the house marinade for the beef and pork and the restaurant's own dipping sauce. The setting is comfortable to sit in, good for a night when you want serious grilled beef rather than roadside mookata.
items.meta: Sirirat Road, Mueang Surin · long-running grilled beef
items.price: Ordered by set/plate, priced to order

items.name: Im Heng Mookata
items.blurb: A mookata buffet that focuses on fresh ingredients rotated daily. You order by scanning a QR code at the table, which is handy — no walking over to serve yourself. The per-head price is reasonable, good for coming as a group or bringing the whole family to sit for a while.
items.meta: Mueang Surin · order via QR at the table

items.name: Khun Sa Grilled Beef (Prasat area)
items.blurb: A pay-by-weight grilled-beef spot for people who want to focus on the meat. You're charged by the weight you order, with free refillable soup and dipping sauce, and they also do off-site party catering. Good for people who don't eat a huge amount but want to pick quality cuts without committing to a buffet.
items.meta: Prasat area, Surin · priced by weight

items.name: Khun Thawee Grilled Beef (by Chang Phueak Canal)
items.blurb: A grilled-beef spot along Chang Phueak Canal, charged by the weight you order, with free unlimited soup and dipping sauce. The canalside setting is cool and pleasant in the evening, good for a night when you want to pick your own cuts and pay for what you actually eat rather than commit to a buffet.
items.meta: By Chang Phueak Canal, Mueang Surin · priced by weight

items.name: Big Ben Korean BBQ
items.blurb: A Korean-BBQ option that's been around a while in Surin, with several sets and sizes to match your group. You don't always have to commit to a buffet, which suits a table of two or three who want Korean-style BBQ without paying a lot.

items.name: Tid Man Hot-Pan BBQ Buffet
items.blurb: A hot-pan grilled-BBQ buffet in town with a wide spread — pork, beef, seafood, and fried items. The room feels newer than roadside mookata, good for a dinner where you want to sit a bit more comfortably and eat for a long time as a group.

items.name: Vintage Mookata (canalside)
items.blurb: A canalside mookata spot open late until around 3am. What people like is the tender marinated pork and the chilled riverside vibe. Good for night owls who get hungry after midnight or want to keep sitting after other places close — an option you don't find often in a provincial town.
items.meta: Canalside, Mueang Surin · open until around 3am

items.name: Grilled skewers at the evening markets
items.blurb: If you don't want a full buffet meal, the evening markets and night markets in Surin usually have grilled pork, grilled chicken, and grilled pork collar sold by the skewer. Buy a few as a snack or take them back to your hotel, paying for what you eat. Good for a night eating solo or as a pair without firing up a whole grill.
items.price: From ฿10–25 per skewer, pay as you eat

blocks.title: Tips for getting the best value
blocks.html: A mookata buffet is best value when you come as a group and plan to eat for a while. If it's just two of you or you don't eat much, pay-by-weight spots like Khun Thawee or Khun Sa, or grilled skewers at the markets, usually work out cheaper. Look for places with "no time limit" like Tang Tao or Mik, because a long, chatty dinner is better value than a place that runs a clock.

blocks.text: What you'll actually pay per head

blocks.html: Most mookata buffets in Surin land in the ฿149–199 per-head range, including vegetables, soup, and dipping sauce. Popular spots like Tang Tao and Mik run around ฿168 with drinks included. Pay-by-weight grilled-beef places charge by what you order — for example, the Prasat-area spot is around ฿239 per kilo, and if you don't eat much you might pay less than a buffet. These are rough ranges from what the shops post themselves and may shift with promotions and festival periods, so it's worth checking the shop's page before you go every time.

items: Group of 4 or more — buffet is the best value; well under ฿200 a head still gets you stuffed
Two of you — if you don't eat much, pay-by-weight or skewers may be cheaper than a buffet
Want to focus on meat — Khun Sa or Khun Thawee charge by weight, so you can pick good cuts without committing to a set price
With small kids — many places price kids by height, and some let those under the threshold eat free; ask at the counter first

blocks.text: What time to go and do you need to book

blocks.html: Most mookata spots in Surin open in the late afternoon, from around 3 to 4pm onward, and the crowds build between 6 and 8pm. At popular spots like Tang Tao and Mik behind Rajabhat, tables fill fast on Friday and Saturday nights, so if you're coming as a big group, try calling to book or arriving before 7pm to make it easier. For a late-night fix after midnight, Vintage Mookata by the canal stays open until around 3am — an option you don't find often outside the big cities.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Prices and opening hours at mookata spots change often, since many are family businesses that mainly post updates on their Facebook page. Before you head out, search the shop's name plus "Surin" and look at the latest post and fresh food photos — that's more reliable than trusting an old price. Some places also run deals that change by the day.

faq.q: Which Surin mookata spot is the most popular?
faq.a: The names locals mention most are Tang Tao Mookata Buffet by the Elephant Show grounds and Mik Grilled Beef Buffet behind Surin Rajabhat. Both are buffets around ฿168 with no time limit on your table, good for a group dinner. For old-school grilled beef, Ruean Racha on Sirirat Road is a town legend.

faq.q: How much does a mookata buffet cost in Surin?
faq.a: Most run ฿149–199 per head, including vegetables, soup, and dipping sauce. Popular spots like Tang Tao and Mik are around ฿168 with drinks included. Pay-by-weight grilled-beef places like Khun Sa are around ฿239 per kilo, and if you don't eat much you might pay less than a buffet. Prices may change with promotions.

faq.q: Is there Korean BBQ or grilled beef in Surin?
faq.a: Yes — for example, Big Ben Korean BBQ has been around a while and offers several sets by group size. For pay-by-weight grilled beef there's Khun Sa in the Prasat area and Khun Thawee by Chang Phueak Canal, where you pick your own cuts and pay by weight. Good for anyone who wants the meat without committing to a buffet.

faq.q: Which Surin mookata spot is open late?
faq.a: Vintage Mookata by the canal stays open until around 3am, good for night owls who get hungry after midnight or want to keep sitting after other places close. It's a late-night option you don't find often in a provincial town, but check the shop's page before you go, since closing time can shift by the day.

faq.q: Is a mookata buffet worth it for two people?
faq.a: If you eat a lot, sure — but if you don't, pay-by-weight grilled-beef spots like Khun Thawee or Khun Sa, or grilled skewers at the evening markets, usually work out cheaper because you pay for what you actually eat. A buffet is best value when you come as a group of 4 or more and plan to sit and eat for a while.
